commit_message:
[Bindings] Fix change HAL bitmask enums to IntEnums instead of IntFlags (#25223)

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 made MemoryType,
BufferCompatibility, BufferUsage and MemoryAccess nanobind IntFlags. On
Python 3.11.0 to 3.11.3, `MemoryType.HOST_LOCAL |
MemoryType.DEVICE_VISIBLE` then fails with "ValueError: 86 is not a
valid MemoryType".

Drop py::is_flag() from the four enums. As IntEnums they keep
`__index__`, which https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 added,
and `|` and `&` return plain ints, as
they did before.

ci-extra: linux_arm64_clang

---------

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Runtime][Python] Preserve DLPack access and ownership

Sharing CPU tensors through DLPack must preserve the producer's storage,
access permissions, and lifetime. The fixed import defaults cannot express
host or read-only memory, and unchecked shapes and offsets can expose
invalid memory. Allow callers to specify placement and access, validate
metadata before import, and use the buffer protocol to keep NumPy views
within the mapped range and retain their owner. Make capsule consumption
transfer ownership exactly once, reject exports whose permissions legacy
DLPack cannot represent, and avoid discard mappings when exporting
existing contents.

Co-authored-by: Tobias Fuchs <9053039+devtbi@users.noreply.github.com>
Assisted-by: Codex
Signed-off-by: Christopher McGirr <mcgirr@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Runtime][Python] Preserve DLPack access and ownership

Sharing CPU tensors through DLPack must preserve the producer's storage,
access permissions, and lifetime. The fixed import defaults cannot express
host or read-only memory, and unchecked shapes and offsets can expose
invalid memory. Allow callers to specify placement and access, validate
metadata before import, and use the buffer protocol to keep NumPy views
within the mapped range and retain their owner. Make capsule consumption
transfer ownership exactly once, reject exports whose permissions legacy
DLPack cannot represent, and avoid discard mappings when exporting
existing contents.

commit_message:
[Runtime][Python] Preserve DLPack access and ownership

Sharing CPU tensors through DLPack must preserve the producer's storage,
access permissions, and lifetime. The fixed import defaults cannot express
host or read-only memory, and unchecked shapes and offsets can expose
invalid memory. Allow callers to specify placement and access, validate
metadata before import, and use the buffer protocol to keep NumPy views
within the mapped range and retain their owner. Make capsule consumption
transfer ownership exactly once, reject exports whose permissions legacy
DLPack cannot represent, and avoid discard mappings when exporting
existing contents.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Add FP32 packed layouts for Wasm SIMD (#25199)

While compiling FP32 matmuls to Wasm, I noticed that enabling data
tiling wasn't selecting a packed layout because the CPU layout selector
didn't have a Wasm case.

This adds tile choices for Wasm SIMD128. I've added tests for
wasm32/wasm64, including checks that scalar Wasm and FP64 keep their
existing behavior.

commit_message:
[HAL] Memoize allocator selects in program order

MemoizeDeviceSelection processed its select groups in DenseMap order,
which follows attribute addresses, so the names of the generated globals
(`__allocator_select_device` vs `_device_0`, etc) changed between runs
and `.vmfb` files of multi-device modules were not reproducible. This
does not affect correctness, only the reproducibility of `.vmfb`
files.

The fix uses a MapVector to process the groups in the order of their
first select.

The lit test now checks exact names instead of capturing them with `.*`.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>

commit_message:
[HAL][bazel] Support external HAL drivers in Bazel (#25238)

Bazel builds can now include HAL drivers from outside IREE.
This matches IREE_EXTERNAL_HAL_DRIVERS in CMake.

The feature is opt-in.
Any module that depends on IREE can add external_hal_driver tags
to iree_extension in its MODULE.bazel.
Each tag names a registration target and a register function.
An optional enabled_by config_setting turns a driver on only for some
builds.

iree_extension collects the tags of all modules.
It generates the @iree_external_hal_drivers repository with the driver
list.
Without tags, the list is empty and the build is unchanged.

A new rule generates init_external.c from init_external.c.in.
The generated file calls each enabled register function.
The drivers library links the enabled targets and compiles
init_external.c.
It also sets IREE_HAVE_HAL_EXTERNAL_DRIVERS, so init.c calls the
generated code.

The new EXTERNAL_DRIVERS.md explains how to opt in.

commit_message:

Bazel builds can now include HAL drivers from outside IREE.
This matches IREE_EXTERNAL_HAL_DRIVERS in CMake.

The feature is opt-in.
Any module that depends on IREE can add external_hal_driver tags
to iree_extension in its MODULE.bazel.
Each tag names a registration target and a register function.
An optional enabled_by config_setting turns a driver on only for some
builds.

iree_extension collects the tags of all modules.
It generates the @iree_external_hal_drivers repository with the driver
list.
Without tags, the list is empty and the build is unchanged.

A new rule generates init_external.c from init_external.c.in.
The generated file calls each enabled register function.
The drivers library links the enabled targets and compiles
init_external.c.
It also sets IREE_HAVE_HAL_EXTERNAL_DRIVERS, so init.c calls the
generated code.

The new EXTERNAL_DRIVERS.md explains how to opt in.

commit_message:
[HAL][bazel] Support external HAL drivers in Bazel (#25238)

Bazel builds can now include HAL drivers from outside IREE.
This matches IREE_EXTERNAL_HAL_DRIVERS in CMake.

The feature is opt-in.
Any module that depends on IREE can add external_hal_driver tags
to iree_extension in its MODULE.bazel.
Each tag names a registration target and a register function.
An optional enabled_by config_setting turns a driver on only for some
builds.

iree_extension collects the tags of all modules.
It generates the @iree_external_hal_drivers repository with the driver
list.
Without tags, the list is empty and the build is unchanged.

A new rule generates init_external.c from init_external.c.in.
The generated file calls each enabled register function.
The drivers library links the enabled targets and compiles
init_external.c.
It also sets IREE_HAVE_HAL_EXTERNAL_DRIVERS, so init.c calls the
generated code.

The new EXTERNAL_DRIVERS.md explains how to opt in.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Split constants larger than the max allocation size

A constant whose storage exceeds the max allocation size of its resource
config cannot be packed within that limit. PackConstants places such
constants in a separate resource, but the size will still exceed the limit.
The problem only shows up at runtime, when the device fails to allocate
the buffer.

This adds `iree-global-opt-split-large-constants`. It splits a private,
immutable global with an inline dense value above the limit into shards
along its outermost non-unit dimension. Each resulting shard is a contiguous
byte range of the original constant and fits into one allocation. The uses
of its loads are rewritten to use the shards:

* An input of a structured op whose split dimension is indexed by a single
  loop: the op is split along that loop with TilingInterface, one op per
  shard. The results of a parallel loop are inserted into the destination.
  The ops of a reduction loop accumulate into the previous result. This
  covers matmuls with a large weight, such as a tied LM head.
* A value read with `tensor.extract` in the body of an elementwise
  `linalg.generic`, e.g., an embedding lookup: a chain of ops, one per
  shard. Each reads its shard at the rebased, clamped index and keeps the
  previous op's element unless the index lies in its shard.

A constant with any other use is left unchanged with a warning, as is one
that cannot be split: mutable or public globals, values that are not inline
dense constants (e.g. parameters), element types not stored at 8, 16, 32 or
64 bits, or a single index of the split dimension that alone exceeds the
limit.

The limit is the max allocation size from `ResourceConfigAttr::lookup`, so
`--iree-stream-resource-max-allocation-size` unless the target sets one. It
defaults to INT64_MAX, so the pass changes nothing unless a limit is set. The
pass runs after transposes have been folded into their consumers, so that an
oversized constant is read by the op that indexes it, and before constant
expressions are hoisted and evaluated into new globals.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Split constants larger than the max allocation size

A constant whose storage exceeds the max allocation size of its resource
config cannot be packed within that limit. PackConstants places such
constants in a separate resource, but the size will still exceed the limit.
The problem only shows up at runtime, when the device fails to allocate
the buffer.

This adds `iree-global-opt-split-large-constants`. It splits a private,
immutable global with an inline dense value above the limit into shards
along its outermost non-unit dimension. Each resulting shard is a contiguous
byte range of the original constant and fits into one allocation. The uses
of its loads are rewritten to use the shards:

* An input of a structured op whose split dimension is indexed by a single
  loop: the op is split along that loop with TilingInterface, one op per
  shard. The results of a parallel loop are inserted into the destination.
  The ops of a reduction loop accumulate into the previous result. This
  covers matmuls with a large weight, such as a tied LM head.
* A value read with `tensor.extract` in the body of an elementwise
  `linalg.generic`, e.g., an embedding lookup: a chain of ops, one per
  shard. Each reads its shard at the rebased, clamped index and keeps the
  previous op's element unless the index lies in its shard.

A constant with any other use is left unchanged with a warning, as is one
that cannot be split: mutable or public globals, values that are not inline
dense constants (e.g. parameters), element types not stored at 8, 16, 32 or
64 bits, or a single index of the split dimension that alone exceeds the
limit.

The limit is the max allocation size from `ResourceConfigAttr::lookup`, so
`--iree-stream-resource-max-allocation-size` unless the target sets one. It
defaults to INT64_MAX, so the pass changes nothing unless a limit is set. The
pass runs after transposes have been folded into their consumers, so that an
oversized constant is read by the op that indexes it, and before constant
expressions are hoisted and evaluated into new globals.

byte range of the original constant and fits into one allocation. The uses
of its loads are rewritten to use the shards:

* An input of a structured op whose split dimension is indexed by a single
  loop: the op is split along that loop with TilingInterface, one op per
  shard. The results of a parallel loop are inserted into the destination.
  The ops of a reduction loop accumulate into the previous result. This
  covers matmuls with a large weight, such as a tied LM head.
* A value read with `tensor.extract` in the body of an elementwise
  `linalg.generic`, e.g., an embedding lookup: a chain of ops, one per
  shard. Each reads its shard at the rebased, clamped index and keeps the
  previous op's element unless the index lies in its shard.

A constant with any other use is left unchanged with a warning, as is one
that cannot be split: mutable or public globals, values that are not inline
dense constants (e.g. parameters), element types not stored at 8, 16, 32 or
64 bits, or a single index of the split dimension that alone exceeds the
limit.

The limit is the max allocation size from `ResourceConfigAttr::lookup`, so
`--iree-stream-resource-max-allocation-size` unless the target sets one. It
defaults to INT64_MAX, so the pass changes nothing unless a limit is set. The
pass runs after transposes have been folded into their consumers, so that an
oversized constant is read by the op that indexes it, and before constant
expressions are hoisted and evaluated into new globals.

commit_message:
[StableHLO] Add plugin registration for composite and custom-call rewrites (#25067)

Compiler plugins need to recognize StableHLO composites and custom calls
before input conversion removes their identity. Add a TargetRegistry and
preprocessing pipeline helper through the existing compiler plugin hook.

Composite handlers register by exact name and version; custom-call
handlers register by target name. Passes own immutable registry
snapshots, and registrations can declare the dialects their handlers
create.

Handlers receive the original operation, including all operands and
regions. They validate applicability before modifying IR and leave IR
unchanged when declining. Remaining composites retain their
decomposition fallback. Custom calls with effects, aliases, tokens, or
futures are excluded from registered dispatch.

The preprocessing helper checks for unsupported mixed StableHLO/VHLO
input, deserializes VHLO, and runs registered rewrites before ordinary
input conversion.

This provides the specialization point used by PyTorch → TorchAX exports
to preserve operations such as attention and quantization through
StableHLO lowering. Mutable model buffers remain explicit state inputs
and outputs; buffer donation enables storage reuse independently of
composite specialization.

This PR supplies the registry and preprocessing infrastructure.
Producer-specific handlers and alias-support opt-in are separate
changes. Tests cover registry ownership and matching, preprocessing,
original operand/region preservation, and chained declines followed by
decomposition fallback.

Compiler plugins need to recognize StableHLO composites and custom calls
before input conversion removes their identity. Add a TargetRegistry and
preprocessing pipeline helper through the existing compiler plugin hook.

Composite handlers register by exact name and version; custom-call
handlers register by target name. Passes own immutable registry
snapshots, and registrations can declare the dialects their handlers
create.

Handlers receive the original operation, including all operands and
regions. They validate applicability before modifying IR and leave IR
unchanged when declining. Remaining composites retain their
decomposition fallback. Custom calls with effects, aliases, tokens, or
futures are excluded from registered dispatch.

The preprocessing helper checks for unsupported mixed StableHLO/VHLO
input, deserializes VHLO, and runs registered rewrites before ordinary
input conversion.

This provides the specialization point used by PyTorch → TorchAX exports
to preserve operations such as attention and quantization through
StableHLO lowering. Mutable model buffers remain explicit state inputs
and outputs; buffer donation enables storage reuse independently of
composite specialization.

This PR supplies the registry and preprocessing infrastructure.
Producer-specific handlers and alias-support opt-in are separate
changes. Tests cover registry ownership and matching, preprocessing,
original operand/region preservation, and chained declines followed by
decomposition fallback.

Assisted-by: codex

---------

Signed-off-by: Jelle Schuhmacher <schuehmacher@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Compiler][API] Bind plugin activation options (#25226)

Embedded sessions have a private option binder, but plugin activation
options were registered only with the global command line. Expose them
through the session binder so C and Python API callers can select
plugins without initializing global CLI state, while library loading
remains a separate initialization step.

Assisted-by: Codex

commit_message:
[CI] Use the Azure sccache in the BYO LLVM build

linux_x64_clang_byollvm still reads the GCS ccache. Nothing has written
to that cache since https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/18511 moved
the Linux jobs to the Azure sccache, so every run builds LLVM, MLIR and
IREE from scratch. The scheduled runs take 3 to 5 hours and sometimes
hit the 6-hour job timeout.

Use the Azure sccache with its own key prefix, like the other jobs on
the cpubuilder_ubuntu_jammy image. byo_llvm.sh always passed ccache as
the compiler launcher. It now uses the launcher from the environment if
one is set. LLVM turns off precompiled headers when the launcher is
sccache.

Without the secret, for example in pull requests from forks,
setup_sccache.sh leaves sccache off and the job uses ccache as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

[CI] Use the Azure sccache in the BYO LLVM build

linux_x64_clang_byollvm still reads the GCS ccache. Nothing has written
to that cache since https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/18511 moved
the Linux jobs to the Azure sccache, so every run builds LLVM, MLIR and
IREE from scratch. The scheduled runs take 3 to 5 hours and sometimes
hit the 6-hour job timeout.

Use the Azure sccache with its own key prefix, like the other jobs on
the cpubuilder_ubuntu_jammy image. byo_llvm.sh always passed ccache as
the compiler launcher. It now uses the launcher from the environment if
one is set. LLVM turns off precompiled headers when the launcher is
sccache.

Without the secret, for example in pull requests from forks,
setup_sccache.sh leaves sccache off and the job uses ccache as before.

commit_message:
[HAL] Support external HAL drivers in Bazel

Bazel builds can now include HAL drivers from outside IREE.
This matches IREE_EXTERNAL_HAL_DRIVERS in CMake.

The feature is opt-in.
Any module that depends on IREE can add external_hal_driver tags
to iree_extension in its MODULE.bazel.
Each tag names a registration target and a register function.
An optional enabled_by config_setting turns a driver on only for some builds.

iree_extension collects the tags of all modules.
It generates the @iree_external_hal_drivers repository with the driver list.
Without tags, the list is empty and the build is unchanged.

A new rule generates init_external.c from init_external.c.in.
The generated file calls each enabled register function.
The drivers library links the enabled targets and compiles init_external.c.
It also sets IREE_HAVE_HAL_EXTERNAL_DRIVERS, so init.c calls the generated code.

The new EXTERNAL_DRIVERS.md explains how to opt in.

Co-Authored-By: Tobias Fuchs <9053039+devtbi@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>

Any module that depends on IREE can add external_hal_driver tags
to iree_extension in its MODULE.bazel.
Each tag names a registration target and a register function.
An optional enabled_by config_setting turns a driver on only for some builds.

iree_extension collects the tags of all modules.
It generates the @iree_external_hal_drivers repository with the driver list.
Without tags, the list is empty and the build is unchanged.

A new rule generates init_external.c from init_external.c.in.
The generated file calls each enabled register function.
The drivers library links the enabled targets and compiles init_external.c.
It also sets IREE_HAVE_HAL_EXTERNAL_DRIVERS, so init.c calls the generated code.

The new EXTERNAL_DRIVERS.md explains how to opt in.

commit_message:
[Bindings] Fix change HAL bitmask enums to IntEnums instead of IntFlags (#25223)

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 made MemoryType,
BufferCompatibility, BufferUsage and MemoryAccess nanobind IntFlags. On
Python 3.11.0 to 3.11.3, `MemoryType.HOST_LOCAL |
MemoryType.DEVICE_VISIBLE` then fails with "ValueError: 86 is not a
valid MemoryType".

Drop py::is_flag() from the four enums. As IntEnums they keep
`__index__`, which https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 added,
and `|` and `&` return plain ints, as
they did before.
